contract.gap: Existing CAD feature-recognition work provides limited evidence for risk-sensitive small-feature recognition and downstream geometry processing on complete heterogeneous aircraft B-Rep models.
contract.task: Recognize rivets and small-features at B-Rep face level and use predictions as candidate inputs to staged CAD processing.
outcomes: per-aircraft error and background false-positive analysis
paired surface-mesh scale and timing comparison

questions.text: Can face geometry and adjacency topology support rivet and small-feature recognition across complete aircraft models?
Can face-level predictions support staged CAD-processing candidates on original and intermediate B-Rep models?

contract.contribution: A face-level graph-learning framework for small-feature recognition on complete-aircraft B-Rep models, with staged CAD-processing candidates and paired mesh comparisons.
nonclaims: No universal generalization claim across all aircraft or CAD sources.
Geometric comparison does not establish physics equivalence.
No CAE acceleration or response-preservation claim before controlled downstream experiments.
No mesh-quality or geometric-fidelity superiority claim over QEM.
Human visual review is not described as fully automatic validation.
Retired BFS and 51-dimensional experiments are not part of the formal model.

facts.value: 48 node features, 6 edge attributes, 4 layers, hidden dimension 64, seed 123, 50 epochs, rivet threshold 0.9, surface threshold 0.5

On 34162 fixed test faces after the documented two-stage CAD screening, the unified three-class classifier obtained background F1=0.9168, rivet F1=0.1312, small-feature F1=0.4589, mIoU=0.4048, and 4762 background false positives.

alignment.method: B-Rep face graph with geometric and topological attributes
alignment.evidence: Complete-aircraft test evaluation, per-aircraft target-class counts and F1, and background false-positive risk
alignment.result: Across 34162 test faces from nine aircraft, rivet F1=0.9312 and small-feature F1=0.8091; 28 rivet and 122 small-feature faces were missed in total, including 103 small-feature faces on Airbus; Air Plane Idea A contributes 82 of 190 background false positives
alignment.interpretation: Face-level recognition is feasible in the reported partition, but pooled metrics do not establish uniform target-class performance across aircraft and residual background false-positive risk remains relevant to downstream processing
alignment.limitation: Some test aircraft may have been used during historical development; limited aircraft and CAD-source diversity

alignment.method: staged CAD removal and local reconstruction
alignment.evidence: Face-level alignment between original-model recognition and CAD-input predictions, nine original--simplified B-Rep pairs, fixed OpenCASCADE meshing controls, and a matched-triangle QEM timing-component baseline
alignment.result: Across the nine pairs, triangle reduction was 0.57--48.66 percent and median meshing-time reduction was 2.49--58.29 percent. At matched triangle targets, final meshing was 7.22--60.05 percent lower than original meshing plus the QEM kernel under the stated limited timing account.
alignment.interpretation: Original-model predictions align face by face across recognition and CAD-input records; the added planar-patch check accounts for the rivet-count difference. The reported pairs have reduced mesh scale and meshing time under the tested controls, without establishing removal completeness, end-to-end superiority, mesh-quality superiority, or engineering-response equivalence.
alignment.limitation: Candidate records do not establish operation-level outcomes; matched-quality QEM comparison and downstream CAE evidence remain unavailable.
alignment.contribution: Downstream CAD-processing candidates and paired mesh comparison

required_fields: paired mesh node and triangle counts
